text: Which type of environment are most suitable for AND–OR trees?

options.text: Unknown environments
Nondeterministic environments
options.note: AND–OR search trees (AIMA §4.3) are built for nondeterministic actions: OR nodes are the agent's choices, AND nodes are the outcomes a plan must cover.

options.text: Online environments
Non-observable environments
options.note: A sensorless (non-observable) problem is solved by ordinary search over belief states; with no percepts there is nothing to branch on, so no AND nodes are needed.

text: Which of the following best describes the sum rule (addition rule) in probability theory?

options.text: It calculates the probability of the intersection of two events.
It determines the probability of the union of two events.
options.note: The addition rule: $P(A \cup B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A \cap B)$, the same formula Question 22 asks for.

options.text: It finds the probability of two independent events occurring together.
options.note: That is the product rule for independent events, $P(A \cap B) = P(A)\,P(B)$.

options.text: It computes the probability of the complement of an event.

text: Which of the following is a limitation of the standard minimax algorithm?

options.text: It is inefficient for games with large search trees due to exhaustive exploration.
options.note: Minimax explores the whole game tree depth-first, $O(b^m)$ time, which is impractical for real games; hence alpha–beta pruning and depth cut-offs.

options.text: It is only applicable to games with imperfect information.
All of the other answers
options.note: Minimax assumes perfect information, so the second option is false, and with it this one.

options.text: It can not easily be adapted to handle games with more than two players.
options.note: Extending minimax to more players is straightforward: each node holds a vector of utilities, one per player (AIMA §5.2).

text: What is the difference between syntax and semantics?

Syntax determines the truth of a sentence in a world, while semantics describes how sentences are formed.
options.note: This swaps the two: syntax is about well-formed sentences, semantics about their truth in each possible world.
